​
He said the project aimed to demonstrate Iran’s scientific capabilities and its ability to compete with leading global powers in advanced technologies.
​
Ali Nowrouzi, head of Iran’s Advanced Technologies Company, explained that nuclear fusion involves bringing two light isotopes together under specific and complex physical conditions to trigger a fusion reaction.
​
He said radiation produced through the process could be used to develop radiopharmaceuticals and advanced medical diagnostic systems.
​
Nowrouzi added that the long-term goal was to develop a system capable of generating high electrical currents without energy losses within the system, underscoring the broader potential of fusion technology for energy production.

🔊 Iranian judoka wins gold at SCO Member States Open Cup in Russia

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iranian judoka Elyas Parhizgar has won a gold medal at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Member States Open Cup, underway in Russia.

The Iranian athlete won a gold medal in the -81 kg category, defeating a Russian opponent in the semifinals and a Tajik judoka in the final.
​
Parhizgar’s triumph marked Iran’s first gold medal at this edition of the tournament.
​
The sporting event, taking place in Moscow and the surrounding region from November 11 to 23, features more than 2,000 athletes representing SCO member states and invited teams, with approximately 100 medal events on the program.
​
Athletes are competing in 11 disciplines, including table tennis, trampoline gymnastics, sambo, sport climbing, artistic and rhythmic gymnastics, weightlifting, fencing, chess, judo and wushu.
​
Iran is represented by a 70-member delegation competing in six sports: sport climbing, judo, weightlifting, artistic gymnastics, chess and table tennis.

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The Islamic Revolution Guards Corps (IRGC) Navy has announced that two oil tankers attempting to pass through unauthorized routes in the Strait of Hormuz exploded after striking naval mines, and one of them sank in the strategic waterway.

According to a statement posted on the IRGC’s official information portal on Sunday, the two offending vessels struck naval mines, triggering powerful explosions in the southern part of the strait in the middle of the day.
​
The statement noted that the tankers—under the deception and with the support of the terrorist US military— had switched off all their identification and positioning systems in an attempt to pass covertly along unauthorized and unsafe routes in the Strait of Hormuz.
​
The IRGC Navy added that one of the vessels—a supertanker carrying over 2 million barrels of crude oil—sank in the southern waters of the Persian Gulf following the explosion and a massive blaze.
​
It further advised fishermen operating in the area to observe safety precautions to avoid colliding with the submerged wreckage of the oil tanker.
​
The statement also warned owners of oil tankers, shipping company executives, and vessel crews against approaching the restricted area of the Strait of Hormuz, urging them not to be misled by the US military.
​
The IRGC Navy reiterated its warnings concerning passage through the area, saying any vessel violating the Iranian regulations governing the Strait of Hormuz—by entering the prohibited and contaminated zone—will face a similar fate.
